articles.title: Barbra Streisand Condemns Trump’s ‘Unchecked Ego’ Over Kennedy Center Name Battle: ‘Galling and Painful to Witness’
articles.summary: Barbra Streisand is speaking out against Pres. Donald Trump’s controversial handling of the Kennedy Center. “In 2008, I was deeply honored to be included in the 31st annual class of Kennedy Center Honorees,” Streisand wrote in a statement posted Thursday on her official website.
body: Streisand’s remarks come on the heels of a district judge ordering the Kennedy Center on Thursday to provide at least 30 days’ notice in advance if a demolition or new construction is planned after Trump threatened that the arts institution could “end up being ripped down” if it didn’t have his support. The Trump administration has been a legal battle to allow the center to be renamed the “Trump-Kennedy Center” after his name be added to the building’s exterior, per board orders. A judge ordered his name be removed.

“Yet the fight continued,” Streisand wrote. “After his name was removed, a humiliated Trump ordered a large tarp placed over the façade, where it remains today. The Trump-aligned board then relentlessly lobbied again to add his name, prompting another federal ruling that blocked their effort.

“And now, a thoroughly defeated Trump has announced that the Kennedy Center is being closed for what the completely stacked board describes as a major renovation,” she continued. “Oddly, when Trump’s name was still on the building, there was no discussion of closing it!”
points: Donald Trump’s controversial handling of the Kennedy Center.

articles.title: Sony TV Chief Keith Le Goy on Why PlayStation 5 FAST Channels Are Set Up for Success: 40-50 Million People ‘Incredibly Engaged With That Platform’
articles.summary: Sony struck synergy gold last month with the introduction of “Live TV on PS5,” an offering of more than 100 free ad-supported video channels available via the PlayStation 5 video game console.
body: Goy added: “So if we can give that audience something that they’re going to like in an environment that they are comfortable with, give our channel partners an audience that they are going to be going after and give their advertisers an audience that’s valuable for them. That is one plus one equaling a lot more than two.”

The PlayStation 5 FAST channel offering launched last month in the U.S. and Goy says the intention is to roll it out across “other countries in the coming months.” Goy sees the option as one unique to Sony, which distinguishes itself from many other players in Hollywood by having film, TV, music and gaming divisions all under one roof.

“In many ways, people talk about the incursion of the tech companies into Hollywood, we were the first and I think we’ve learned a lot along the way,” You mentioned the relationship with PlayStation. “That’s the other thing that Sony has, that frankly a lot of other companies would love to have, is a gaming business and the level of engagement with gamers and gaming fans. articles.title: Dr. Orna Guralnik Gives Ciara Miller, Dylan Efron and Carl Schmidt a ‘Couples Therapy’ Session in New Samsung Galaxy Spot
articles.summary: Samsung is taking its latest Galaxy campaign to therapy. The tech giant has tapped “Couples Therapy” star Dr. Orna Guralnik to lead “Switchers,” a new campaign that centers a counseling session on the anxieties around ditching a longtime smartphone.
body: If you purchase an independently reviewed product or service through a link on our website, Variety may receive an affiliate commission.

“My profession is all about change,” Guralnik, a clinical psychologist who stars in Showtime’s “Couples Therapy,” tells Variety. “People come to analysis when they’ve reached a certain point where they’re just repeating the same old patterns and having a hard time letting go or changing.”

“The fact that Samsung decided to go toward this kind of psychological, even psychoanalytic language — even using language like, ‘What’s your defense?’ — it just tickled me a lot,” Guralnik continues. “What a great way to bring psychoanalytic and psychological language into mass culture, which is really what I’m doing with the show anyhow.”

The commercial is the latest example of Samsung leaning on talent to market its Galaxy lineup. Earlier this year, the company added singer and rapper Audrey Nuna, model and influencer Haley Baylee and 11 other creators across music, gaming, fashion and culture to its #TeamGalaxy roster around the Galaxy S26 launch. Samsung also enlisting K-pop talent including Eric Nam for its Galaxy Experience in February.

articles.title: Why stop at Wuthering Heights: House of the Damned? Bring on Mrs Dalloway’s Rampage!
articles.summary: It isn’t just Winnie the Pooh – now the star of Blood & Honey II. Budget shockers are treating any story with expired copyright as ripe for murderous exploitation. It is significant that, at this point in our cultural journey, we have become accustomed to film producers jumping on every single…
body: But if you zoom out even a tiny amount, it all starts to look a little silly. Not because it suggests the paying public has a fondness for inarguably bad horror films based on loose interpretations of recognisable figures, but because it’s missing the bigger picture. In other words, while producers are watching eagerly for the next newly out-of-copyright property to exploit (by the way, Babar the Elephant will enter the public domain in January), there is an entire ocean of public domain work just sitting there to be desecrated.

In which case, you really have to applaud whoever came up with the idea of Wuthering Heights: The House of the Damned. Available on digital platforms in three short weeks (on 19 October in fact), it is a remake of Emily Brontë’s classic novel, only scarier. In the film, as far as I am able to tell, Cathy has died and her ghost starts haunting Heathcliff to the point that he starts murdering everyone. Is it any good? All signs point to not really, especially since the trailer contains a shot where Cathy seems to become a zombie so that she can punch through a window and strangle someone to death. But will I watch it? Oh God, try to stop me.

articles.title: Marooned Lord Byron statue returns to Hyde Park
articles.summary: The statue was left isolated on a Park Lane traffic island after new roads were built in the 1960s.
body: A statue of the 19th-century poet Lord Byron has been returned to Hyde Park, nearly 70 years after it was isolated on a traffic island when new roads were built through the area in the early 1960s.

The Grade II-listed statue was erected as a national memorial in 1880 after receiving special permission from Queen Victoria. Changes to the Park Lane road layout 80 years later left it inaccessible, leading it to become isolated, neglected and dirty.
The Lord Byron Society launched a campaign to relocate the statue six years ago, arguing it had become neglected.
The move cost more than £400,000, funded by a £230,000 grant from The National Lottery Heritage Fund and additional donations.
points: The statue was left isolated on a Park Lane traffic island after new roads were built in the 1960s.

articles.title: ‘When you tell people the story, it’s almost too good to be true’: the incredible journey behind The Cycle of Love
articles.summary: Documentary director Orlando von Einsiedel on how the real life tale of a man who cycles 6,000 miles from India to Sweden to find his true love will warm your heart. New Delhi, December 1975.
body: New Delhi, December 1975. It was love at first sight when a Swedish hippy called Lotta von Schedvin sat down to be sketched by an Indian street artist, Pradyumna Kumar Mahanandia, known to everyone as PK. In the 10 minutes it took PK to complete her portrait, everything clicked into place for the pair. They were swept headlong in a whirlwind romance, and PK took Lotta to his village in the east of India to meet his family. But soon after, the time came for Lotta to pack up her VW campervan and head back home with her friends.

Heart-stricken PK promised to follow, but a plane ticket to Sweden was an impossible dream. Determined not to lose the love of his life, PK bought a secondhand Raleigh bike, and with $80 sewn into the waistband of his trousers, set off to cycle 6,000 miles to Lotta. He knew the sun set in the west, so that was the direction he took. His plan was to follow the hippy trail, cycling through India, Pakistan, Afghanistan, Iran and Turkey, crossing Europe, finally arriving in Sweden.

articles.title: GTA 6 soundtrack reveal revives digital release debate
articles.summary: Fred Again, PinkPantheress and Travis Scott provide new music for the blockbuster - but not all fans are happy.
body: The reveal of a Grand Theft Auto 6 soundtrack album has reignited a debate over the decision not to release the game on disc.
Developer Rockstar Games announced a 34-track compilation, set to release on CD and vinyl on the same day as the highly anticipated video game.

The company says it will include original music from a "genre-defying roster of the most exciting artists in the world" including rapper Travis Scott, country singer Morgan Wallen and UK singer PinkPantheress.
But some fans have pointed out the "irony" of putting out a physical edition of the album following its controversial decision for a digital-only release of the game.

articles.title: Palace in war of words with Earl Spencer over claims in Diana book
articles.summary: The row threatens to overshadow a very crowded day for the royals - with the King and Princes William and Harry all attending events.
body: Buckingham Palace is in a war of words with Earl Spencer, brother of Diana, Princess of Wales, over a controversial memoir about her life and death.
King Charles III is accused of insensitively telling Earl Spencer, in the wake of Princess Diana's death in 1997, that "we'll forget her soon enough", according to excerpts in the Daily Mail.
But the Palace has pushed back unusually strongly, angered by the claims and attempting to cast doubt on them.

"While we do not comment on books as a matter of principle, His Majesty is mindful that the pain of fraternal grief can cloud reason, affect judgment and colour memory in ways others do not recognise, even many years after such a loss," it said.

articles.title: De Gaulle: Liberté review – biopic of conquering French war hero reaches his imperial era
articles.summary: A shrewd performance by Simon Abkarian leads this blockbuster account of the wartime leader’s career as he ascends to political dominance. The massive and commercially triumphant two-part movie about General Charles de Gaulle comes to end with this second half, which does not, as I half expected it…
body: As before, Abkarian has plenty of scenes where he gets out of military aircraft and haughtily sizes up the reception awaiting him, hyper-alert to tiny slights to his status and thereby to France itself. He cannot enter a room in this film without a moment in which he considers who is there and how they might insult him; Abkarian makes the most of this amusing dark comedy. Perhaps Liberté doesn’t quite have the intrigue and the intimate drama of the first half but it is still a rousingly watchable movie, a French production in the spirit of J Lee Thompson or John Sturges.
